exposure: early anemia (hemoglobin <=145 g/L within the first week after birth)
outcome: neurodevelopment at 1 month corrected age (measured by neonatal behavioral neurological assessments - NBNA)
brain injury within 1 month corrected age (measured by cranial ultrasound)
cohort: The study included 110 very-low-birth-weight (VLBW) preterm infants from Southern China, equally divided into early anemia and non-anemic groups, matched by birth weight and gestational age.
finding: Early anemia in VLBW preterm infants is negatively correlated with neurodevelopment, particularly behavioral ability, but shows no association with brain injury.
